LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 1 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we write legibly and neatly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify features of a good handwriting for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. re-write an essay using neat and legible handwriting for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate neatness and legibility in handwriting.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify features of a good handwriting for effective communication,

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. re-write an essay using neat and legible handwriting for comprehension,

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate neatness and legibility in handwriting.

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on features of a good handwriting with peers,

2. work jointly to note down the various cultural festivals and ceremonies using neat and legible handwriting,

3. work jointly with peers to compose sentences using adverbs,

4. re-write a short essay on the theme in neat and legible handwriting,

5. proofread the written essays with peers,

6. publish their neatly written essays in the school or public magazine.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on features of a good handwriting with peers,
2. work jointly to note down the various cultural festivals and ceremonies using neat and legible handwriting,
3. work jointly with peers to compose sentences using adverbs,
4. re-write a short essay on the theme in neat and legible handwriting,
5. proofread the written essays with peers,
6. publish their neatly written essays in the school or public magazine.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: The learner engages actively using facts and examples to proofread the written

essays with peers.

• Learning to Learn: This is cultivated as the learner engages in collective learning when brainstorming on features of a

good handwriting with peers.

6

Values:
● Responsibility: This is developed as the learner engages in assigned roles and duties when working with peers to compose

sentences using adverbs.

● Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers to note down the various cultural festivals and ceremonies

using neat and legible handwriting.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Cultural awareness: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with indigenous content on various cultural celebrations

and festivals.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concepts on handwriting to their learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili and English.

7

THEME 2: ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION

Suggested Vocabulary: surrounding, conserve, pollute, energy, recycle, preserve, reduce, reuse, trees, rivers,

environment, litter

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify features of a good handwriting for effective communication,
2. re-write an essay using neat and legible handwriting for comprehension,
3. appreciate neatness and legibility in handwriting.

Remember the key question: Why should we write legibly and neatly?
